Class JUnitXmlReportWriter

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.dev.test.JUnitXmlReportWriter
All Implemented Interfaces:
Ordered, TestEventListener, TestReportListener
public final class JUnitXmlReportWriter extends Object implements TestReportListener
Writes the JUnit XML reports of a run, the format CI servers, IDEs and the build tools read: one TEST-<class>.xml per class in the Ant and Surefire shape, a testsuite of testcases with their classname, time, failure, error or skip, and captured system-out and system-err. A test without a class, such as a pytest function, is grouped under its file.

The writer keeps the latest result of every test across the runs it sees, so a report always holds a class's latest results rather than only those of the last run. A complete run of every test with no pattern replaces them all, and removes the reports of classes it did not see, because they were deleted or renamed. A complete run of classes or methods selected by name replaces their results, removing a test that is gone, and the report of a class left with none. Any other run, one filtered by patterns, cancelled, or cut short by the runner, only adds its results, since it says nothing of the tests it did not reach. Results kept are those of this writer's runs: a report an earlier process wrote is replaced when its class runs again. Each report is replaced through a rename, so a reader never sees half a file, and characters XML cannot hold are replaced. The run's selection is recorded as the micronaut.dev.test.selection property, so a reader can tell an affected run from a full one.

    • reportOf

      public Path reportOf(String className)
      The report file of a class: TEST-<class>.xml with the binary name as it is, as Surefire names it. A name that is not a Java binary name, such as a test file's path, is escaped so that two names never share a file: every character but an ASCII letter, a digit, ., _ and $ becomes - and the two hex digits of each of its UTF-8 bytes. A binary name never holds a -, and an escaped name always does, so the two kinds cannot meet. An escaped name too long for a file name, as the absolute path of a deep test file can be, keeps its end, the most telling part, after a hash of the whole name.
      Parameters:
      className - The class, or the file of tests without one
      Returns:
      The file
